scope: Legacy local image reads, stored URL compatibility and release packaging; managed media is inspected only to distinguish current producers.
sourceIdentity: source-reference-inventory.json#sourceManifest; dependency-source-evidence.json for installed Next and dated graph provenance

reviewedTraces.conclusion: These reviewed producers no longer write public/uploads. Provider public-read ACL applies to encrypted managed bytes and does not establish legacy local upload behavior. No provider was contacted.
The /uploads/{org} localStoragePath field survives as configuration metadata. Current update rejects local mode/path changes and does not create upload directories.

Item updates explicitly retain previously stored nonmanaged image references. New item references are checked by claimItemPictures. Deleting an unattached legacy reference is rejected. A repair must not silently delete or rewrite retained images.

API checks fresh session/org, equal path org, dashboard module admission and dashboard.read before reading public/uploads/{org}/{file}; returns private,no-store. It is tenant-scoped, not item/location-scoped. Exact filename grammar is ASCII alphanumeric/dot/underscore/hyphen without '..'; supported jpg/jpeg/png/gif/webp only.

Current middleware bypasses dotted non-API paths and has no upload-specific guard. Release preparation recursively copies all public files, including ignored uploads, into runtime/public. Git-based candidate capture omits ignored untracked uploads. A source fingerprint alone does not attest which legacy private bytes enter the runtime artifact.

Comprehensive seed writes /seed-images assets, not /uploads. audit-picture-storage inventories legacy references across items, categories, brands and users but loads env and opens a DB; it was inspected only, not executed. Current DB prevalence, missing assets and ownership associations remain unknown.

Dynamic item previews/POS use raw stored image URLs in native img; edited item Next/Image explicitly uses unoptimized. AvatarImage accepts avatarUrl. Retaining same-origin legacy URL behavior avoids data rewrites; authenticated cookies must reach the read endpoint. This is source dataflow, not rendered/browser qualification.

Categories accept stored image URL strings; brand writes require absolute URL syntax. Their forms accept URL text. This is reference persistence, not a local file producer. Historical users/category/brand references must remain in the migration/compatibility inventory even though the current item uploader uses managed media.

constraints.requirement: Apply the same current authority decision to /uploads/{org}/{file} and /api/uploads/{org}/{file}; successful direct API tests alone cannot qualify the static URL.
Keep eligible same-org reads byte-identical with correct image MIME and private,no-store. Existing references must not be broken by blocking all uploads indiscriminately.

The legacy API currently uses dashboard.read/dashboard module while managed media uses inventory/POS permissions and corresponding modules. Preserve and explicitly state the chosen existing legacy policy during a bounded repair. Broader item/location privacy or different policy requires a reviewed decision and resource mapping; do not infer it from path organization.

Test raw and percent-encoded path routing at HTTP level: encoded ordinary filename characters, encoded slashes/backslashes/dot segments, double encoding, repeated separators and Unicode/space filenames. Define compatibility for already stored encodings instead of decoding recursively.

Installed Next 15.5.27 internal image fetch uses a fresh request without original headers/cookies; protected image optimization therefore loses session. Keep authenticated consumers unoptimized/native img. A cold optimizer request must expose no bytes; existing public cache entries require explicit invalidation/rebuild evidence. Cache key includes href,width,quality,mimeType, not identity, and optimized response is public-cacheable.

Middleware protection alone does not qualify independently served public files, old runtime artifacts, direct object URLs or cached CDN/optimizer copies. Deny/remove private content from public packaging and verify origin/CDN routing and purge evidence before deployment; never roll back to public exposure.

Legacy path containment must cover real filesystem symlink/junction escape if private storage is introduced. No symlinks were observed in this three-file workspace inventory, but API path.resolve containment alone is not a realpath guarantee.

Reads/denials must not mutate asset bytes or business rows. Module admission with audit:true may intentionally emit security audit evidence; distinguish permitted audit events from forbidden business/asset mutations.

This local metadata snapshot covers 3 JPG files in 1 org directory only. No DB association, external storage, deployed volume, live CDN or cache inventory was accessed. Parent may copy into an explicitly isolated fixture and bind hashes.

repairOptions.description: Place legacy bytes outside any public/static root, route both legacy and API URLs through one shared authenticated read implementation, and fail/exclude private uploads in public artifact packaging. Preserve original URLs and eligible bytes. Prepare a manifest-bound copy/verify/recovery plan; do not automatically move/delete production data.

Rewrite /uploads to the existing guarded API before static dispatch, explicitly cover URI normalization and image optimizer routing, and deny public-file inclusion/direct static hosting. If bytes remain public and independent origin/CDN serving is possible, this cannot close the full production gate.

Migrate retained legacy references to managed media using independently verified ownership, cryptographic byte checks and reversible reference mapping. This is broader data work with provider and approval gates; it is not necessary for the first isolated two-URL qualification and is not authorized by this source inventory.

testMatrix.case: Anonymous GET of each fixture through both URL forms
testMatrix.acceptance: Denied status; response contains no fixture byte sequence and hash differs from asset; no filesystem asset changes.

testMatrix.case: Authenticated tenant B requests tenant A asset through both URL forms
testMatrix.acceptance: 403 or equivalent deny; zero private image bytes; no forbidden writes.

testMatrix.case: Tenant A with current required permission and module reads all eligible same-org fixtures through both URL forms
testMatrix.acceptance: 200, exact SHA-256 equality, matching MIME/length, nosniff, private,no-store; preserves valid reads.

testMatrix.case: Expired then revoked sessions reuse both URLs
testMatrix.acceptance: Fresh authentication denies; no image bytes. Stub-only contexts must be labeled and do not prove revocation.

testMatrix.case: Remove dashboard.read or deny dashboard module after successful read
testMatrix.acceptance: Next request denies both URLs without private bytes, even when cookies/URLs are unchanged; capture allowed audit separately.

testMatrix.case: Benign percent encoding of admitted filename characters
testMatrix.acceptance: Both URL forms normalize once and either return authorized exact bytes consistently or reject by an explicit compatibility rule; anonymous/foreign requests remain denied.

testMatrix.case: Encoded traversal/slashes/backslashes, double encoding, malformed escapes, extra/missing segments, query suffix and repeated separators
testMatrix.acceptance: No path escapes, alternate public dispatch or bytes from a nonadmitted file; deny/error responses contain no filesystem paths or secrets.

testMatrix.case: Missing supported asset, unsupported extension, mixed-case permitted extension
testMatrix.acceptance: Defined safe 404/400 or successful valid read; both URLs keep equivalent authority and MIME policy.

testMatrix.case: HEAD, Range, conditional ETag/If-Modified-Since on allowed and denied contexts
testMatrix.acceptance: No body/private byte disclosure for denied contexts; no 206/304 cache bypass; permitted behavior documented without relying on GET-only unit mocks.

testMatrix.case: Cold /_next/image?url=<encoded legacy URL>&w=...&q=... for both aliases; allowed then anonymous/foreign repeat
testMatrix.acceptance: No unauthenticated image delivery. Protected browser images render through native img/unoptimized. Cache effects measured and clearly separated from original-byte comparison because optimization transforms bytes.

testMatrix.case: Fixture cache warmed under old public route, then candidate repair
testMatrix.acceptance: Cached private image cannot be fetched after cutover; require purge/new cache namespace plus evidence for origin/edge caches before production admission.

testMatrix.case: Prepare candidate from synthetic public/uploads sentinel and inspect sealed runtime/public manifest
testMatrix.acceptance: No private legacy bytes publicly packaged; pipeline rejects or redirects to private manifest-bound storage. Candidate source hash and artifact file hash coverage explicitly reconciled.

testMatrix.case: Symlink/junction fixture pointing beyond allowed org root when supported
testMatrix.acceptance: Read denied; external sentinel unread. Skip with limitation if platform privileges prevent fixture creation.

testMatrix.case: Item edit, upload preview, item list, POS thumbnail/dialog and legacy avatar fixture
testMatrix.acceptance: Eligible images render with session cookies; foreign/private images fail without leaked bytes; no image optimizer credential loss or broken legitimate thumbnails.

testMatrix.case: Private copy interrupted before/after verification, missing file, rollback
testMatrix.acceptance: No loss/overwrite of original bytes; resume by manifest/hash; maintain deny boundary during recovery; never restore public exposure as rollback.

existingTestsInspectedNotExecuted.coverage: 7 mocked route tests cover session, tenant, module, permission, traversal, extension and allowed API read; filesystem/auth/NextResponse are mocked; no legacy static URL, real cookies, Next optimizer, HTTP encoding, deployment or CDN coverage.
Retained legacy reference compatibility is asserted; no deployed file read.
Mixed managed and retained legacy image references are asserted.
New unmanaged legacy import references are rejected.

advancementEvidence: A candidate source digest, copied-fixture manifest and runtime identity for the explicitly isolated test target.
Per-URL denial response/body checks and valid-read byte/hash checks; status codes alone are insufficient.
Explicit auth-adapter/mock inventory: an isolated harness using stubbed sessions qualifies route composition only, not real session revocation.
Independent review of implementation and test observations; unresolved cache, deployment, DB inventory and permission-policy decisions remain blocked/deferred explicitly.
